title: macOS Big Sur interface
lede: Apple’s 2020 desktop redesign: frosted Control Center tiles and notifications over a vivid wave wallpaper.
summary: Translucent, blurred Control Center and notifications over a saturated wallpaper. Apple, 2020.

evidence.note: Inspected two Apple Newsroom press images in scratchpad copies: the Control Center close-up (apple_macos-bigsur_controlcenter_06222020, 1306 × 1306) and the Notification Center close-up (apple_macos-bigsur_notificationcenter_06222020, 1306 × 1306). Not stored. The operating system was not run.

styles.note: Malewicz’s naming article and Everyday UX both name Big Sur as the moment the style entered a mainstream desktop. Its Control Center matches every diagnostic trait.

context: Apple’s press release describes a menu bar with “a new translucent material”, an all-new Control Center, and a redesigned Notification Center with widgets. [Apple Newsroom](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2020/06/apple-introduces-macos-big-sur-with-a-beautiful-new-design/).

Wikipedia says Big Sur “features new blurs to establish a visual hierarchy” and was the first macOS user interface redesign since OS X Yosemite. [Wikipedia: macOS Big Sur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MacOS_Big_Sur).

Malewicz writes that Apple “recently brought transparent-blurs back with Mac OS Big Sur” and suggests that this may be why Apple chose a colorful default wallpaper. [Malewicz 2020](ref:malewicz-glassmorphism-article-2020).
observed: The wallpaper is a set of large, smooth waves in blue, white, orange, red, and magenta.
Control Center is one large translucent panel with rounded corners. Inside it, tiles for Wi-Fi, Do Not Disturb, Display, Sound, and Now Playing are lighter translucent rounded rectangles.
The blue and orange of the wallpaper show through the panel as soft color. No wallpaper edges are sharp behind it.
Sliders are white pills on a darker translucent track. Controls use flat blue discs and SF-style sans-serif text.
Notification cards are translucent blue-tinted rounded rectangles. The widgets below them are opaque white or dark grey, so both treatments appear side by side.
interpretation: Big Sur’s Control Center is the clearest large-platform example of the web recipe: glass inside glass, flat content, and a wallpaper chosen to make the blur visible. The opaque widgets show the rule of opacity for hierarchy.
borrow: Nest lighter translucent tiles inside a translucent panel to group controls without borders.
Pair glass surfaces with a wallpaper of large, smooth color areas, not a detailed photo.

rights.statement: Apple press images and software; copyrighted. No image is stored here.
